clue.text: Opera that gave a conductor his start

definitions.text: Opera that gave a conductor his start

parts.words: Opera that gave a conductor his start
parts.note: a Puccini opera whose title forms the opening five letters of the surname of the great Italian conductor Arturo ...

explanation.surface: An opera house remembers the work in which a famous conductor made his debut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gave a conductor his start' reads as a debut story, but the start meant is the first five letters of Toscanini's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera about the singer Floria is a famous Italian work, and its title begins the conductor Toscanini's surname.

clue.text: Wear for an athlete-as well as a plate-layer ?

definitions.meaning: a loose warm outfit worn by runners
a plate-layer is a British railway worker who lays the rails, so the railway lines suit him

explanation.surface: A sports outfit is said to suit a railway worker too.
explanation.definitionFit: Running gear is athletes' clothing; and a man who lays rails would find that rails were his line, the second reading taken in two words.

clue.text: Try as one might to reform a somewhat beastly type

indicators.note: reform says the letters of 'try as' are formed afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: However hard one tries, a brute cannot be reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One might' is padding in the surface; 'Try as' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodland god of Greek myth was part man, part goat, so only partly an animal.

clue.text: Moloch's worshippers are old fossils

definitions.meaning: a Biblical people east of the Jordan whose god was Moloch
extinct coiled-shell sea creatures found as fossils

explanation.surface: The followers of a pagan god are dismissed as old fogeys.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical people of Ammon served the god Moloch; and coiled shells of extinct molluscs are common fossils.

clue.text: Means of sharing communication of official policy

definitions.meaning: a telephone line shared by several subscribers, who could overhear one another
the stance a political party expects all its members to repeat

explanation.surface: Someone describes how the government gets its official message across.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are fixed phrases: a shared telephone connection, and the agreed position of a political party.

clue.text: Sulky-like Gray's Selima ?

definitions.meaning: peevish, bad-tempered
Selima was the pet cat in Thomas Gray's ode on her drowning, so like a pet is read as pet plus the suffix -ish

explanation.surface: Thomas Gray's famous cat is called sulky.
explanation.definitionFit: Peevish means sulky; and the poet's drowned cat was a household pet, hence 'pet-ish'.

clue.text: Operated old radio show in Burma

definitions.note: the definition names a city in Burma, so it stands for a place there

parts.note: ran means operated, as a machine is run
The Goon Show was a 1950s BBC radio comedy

explanation.surface: Someone ran an old radio programme while stationed in Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: The former capital of Burma, now called Yangon, is its main city.

clue.text: The age of Virginia Woolf

definitions.meaning: a long time, as in 'it took ages'
a 1937 novel by Virginia Woolf takes this word as its title

explanation.surface: Someone asks how old Virginia Woolf was.
explanation.definitionFit: A long time is an age; and Woolf wrote a family-saga novel with this title.

clue.text: Resistance of one member to oriental measure

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
MP is a Member of Parliament
E is east, oriental
a measure is an old word for a dance

explanation.surface: An MP resists an eastern measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' reads politically but is the electrical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In electrics, opposition to alternating current is measured in ohms.

clue.text: Hemingway's last letter dropped by eagles

indicators.note: the final letter of his first name is dropped from the end

parts.note: Ernest was the novelist Hemingway's first name

explanation.surface: Hemingway's final letter is dropped by eagles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last letter' sounds like the writer's final correspondence; it means the final letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Erne is an old name for the sea eagle, common in crosswords.

clue.text: Industrial technique I left to this robot

indicators.note: the letter for 'I' is left out of the longer word, so it departs

parts.note: the use of machines to run factory processes with little human labour

explanation.surface: A worker complains that a factory method has left him behind in favour of a robot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like 'abandoned', the worker's fate, but it tells you to drop I from AUTOMATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that moves and works by itself, like a mechanical man, is the classic self-operating device.

clue.text: Like the writer-popular but non-U

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of 'in the manner of'
a pen is what a writer writes with, standing for the writer

explanation.surface: A writer is described as popular but not upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself cryptic: POPULAR without its U is POPLAR, and the answer is a kind of poplar. 'Non-U' also means 'not upper-class', the surface's reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The quaking tree with trembling leaves belongs to the poplar genus, Populus.

clue.text: She produces new edition of Ranke

definitions.note: a woman's first name stands for 'she'

indicators.note: a new edition reworks a book, so the name Ranke is reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman is responsible for revising the works of the historian Ranke.
explanation.walkthrough: Leopold von Ranke was a German historian, which makes a 'new edition' plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name stands in for any woman, referred to as 'she'.

clue.text: TV chief's old soldiers

definitions.meaning: Ironside was the wheelchair-using police chief of a 1960s-70s TV detective series; with the possessive the name gains an S
Cromwell's cavalry in the English Civil War were nicknamed after his own 'Old' nickname

explanation.surface: Someone talks about the veterans who once served under a television police chief.
explanation.definitionFit: The TV detective's name plus its possessive matches the nickname of Oliver Cromwell's seventeenth-century troopers.

clue.text: Disconnect wagon perhaps, causing a French hold-up

parts.note: un is French for 'a'
a hitch is a delay or snag

explanation.surface: Uncoupling a wagon causes a delay for a French traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' suggests a robbery of the wagon; it is just a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a wagon from the horse or vehicle pulling it is to detach its coupling.

clue.text: Greets colour with precipitation

parts.note: to hail is to greet
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A painter greets a shade of colour with downpours.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice falling from a cloud is a form of precipitation.

clue.text: Peppercorn rent, so-called

definitions.meaning: a token rent, far below real value
existing in name only

explanation.surface: A tenant pays a token rent that hardly deserves the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A token sum is one in name only, and so-called means named but not really so.

clue.text: Mary at college in Cambridge

definitions.meaning: Mary ..., the follower of Jesus
one of the Cambridge University colleges, pronounced 'maudlin'

explanation.surface: Mary is studying at a Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary of Magdala followed Jesus; and a Cambridge college bears her name, said 'maudlin'.

clue.text: Subsequent partner on the side

parts.note: later means subsequent
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A later partner is someone on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideways or from the side, as a lateral pass goes.

clue.text: Viola or Sebastian went down to get knitwear

parts.note: the separated brother and sister in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night are twins
the sun set, meaning went down

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character goes down to fetch a cardigan.
explanation.walkthrough: A twinset is a matching jumper and cardigan worn together, a classic British women's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching jumper and cardigan sold as a pair is a knitted outfit.

clue.text: Put your foot down on hobo taking pound note

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone steps on a vagrant who has taken a pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush underfoot is to tread heavily on something.

clue.text: The greedy chap, we hear, imported dyestuff

parts.note: a greedy person is called a pig

indicators.note: says the next word is spoken, and only its sound is entered in the grid

parts.note: to import is to signify, so imported means meant

explanation.surface: A greedy man, by repute, brought dye into the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imported' looks like trade but means 'signified'; the word for it, said aloud, is the ending of the dyestuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that gives colour to paint or fabric is a colouring matter.

clue.text: She's versed in literature

parts.note: a woman described as knowledgeable about books, but 'versed' means writing in verse

explanation.surface: A well-read woman is praised.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who writes verse is a female poet.

clue.text: A drink for the parson at rustic opera

parts.note: a pastor is a clergyman
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A parson is given a drink while watching a country opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link here, though it tempts a solver to look for a substitution; the drink simply follows the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical piece or stage work on a country theme, about shepherds and rural life.

clue.text: Softly sounded the crash

parts.note: p is piano, softly in music
a bell rang, meaning sounded

explanation.surface: The crash came with only a soft noise.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a crash, especially a car or plane accident.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a minor car or plane accident.

clue.text: A rumour, as one says in France

definitions.meaning: a piece of gossip
the French for 'one says' or 'they say'

explanation.surface: A rumour, as the French put it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay or gossip; literally the French for 'they say'.

clue.text: Like the Lady's tribe

parts.note: as means like
her is the possessive for a lady

explanation.surface: A woman is said to resemble her own tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: Asher was one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the twelve tribes of Israel, named after a son of Jacob.

clue.text: Adopt a better method of insurance

definitions.text: Adopt a better method of insurance

parts.words: Adopt a better method of insurance
parts.note: a 'better' is one who bets, and protecting against losses by betting on both sides is the gambler's insurance

explanation.surface: Someone advises switching to a superior insurance policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'better' as 'one who bets': guarding a wager by also backing the other side is to hedge one's bets.
explanation.definitionFit: To protect oneself against loss by covering both outcomes of a bet.

clue.text: Shun what is naturally abhorrent?

definitions.meaning: to keep away from
the saying 'nature abhors a vacuum': an empty space, written as two words

explanation.surface: Keep away from something nature finds repugnant.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep away from is to steer clear; and an empty space is what the proverb says nature abhors.

clue.text: Oddly enough, Pearl goes round the bend about clerical, stipends

indicators.note: the rearranged name goes round the other piece, enclosing it
oddly says the letters of Pearl behave strangely and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Pearl is driven mad by the matter of church payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes round the bend' means 'goes mad', but 'goes round' is a container signal. A prebend is the stipend a cathedral canon drew from church revenues.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a prebend, the income a cathedral canon drew from church estates.

clue.text: The size of no minor promontory

parts.note: something no minor is great, large
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Someone notes how big a certain headland is.
explanation.definitionFit: Largeness or magnitude, the quality of being big.

clue.text: Man of morality

parts.note: the fifteenth-century English morality play whose hero represents all humanity: the word that comes before 'man' in its title

explanation.surface: A virtuous man is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of morality' looks like a good person; it is the word that precedes 'Man' in the title of the morality play.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval play's title character stands for all mankind, each and every person.
